newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy coalition partners ask for govt meeting.
newsitem.headline: Italy coalition partners ask for govt meeting.

text.p: The parliamentary party leaders of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) on Wednesday asked Prime Minister Romano Prodi to a hold a meeting of coalition partners to discuss the planned mini-budget.
Prodi said earlier that he and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi had already worked out a framework for an eventual package of measures although the exact size of the budget was not yet known.
Fabio Mussi and Cesare Salvi wrote to Prodi to ask for a meeting of all coalition allies.
"Once the government has formally announced that there will be a budget it is politically necessary to talk about this with the parliamentary majority," Mussi told reporters.
The two parliamentary leaders representing the largest group within the centre-left coalition, said they backed government aims but added that Prodi needed to secure a single position in parliament.
The hard left Communist Refoundation, which guarantees the government's majority in the lower house of parliament, said on Wednesday it did not see the need for a mini-budget.
It said it was prepared to talk about the package but only on the understanding that any eventual budget did not increase taxes or cut state spending. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
